report.summary: The release adds interactive prompting and updates how logger instances are created, with prompt behavior varying between terminal and browser use.
keyChanges: Logger instances can now provide prompts, including text entry, confirmation, single selection, and multiple selection; testers can exercise these prompt types in the supplied example.
Browser prompts use the browser’s native confirmation dialog for confirmations and its text dialog for other prompt types, so selection options are not presented as an interactive choice list there.
Logger creation now supports caller-supplied reporter options while retaining environment-based defaults when none are supplied.
qaChecks: Verify the text prompt starts with “java” and accepts entered text.
Check the confirmation prompt returns a yes-or-no choice.
Confirm the single-selection prompt presents both repeated “TypeScript” entries and “CoffeeScript” as options.
Ensure the optional multi-selection prompt allows submitting with no tools selected.
Verify a confirmation prompt opens the browser’s native confirmation dialog.
uncertainty: The supplied evidence does not show the previous prompt implementation, so it cannot establish a concrete input that took a different path before this release.

checks: Verify the text prompt starts with “java” and accepts entered text.
Check the confirmation prompt returns a yes-or-no choice.
Confirm the single-selection prompt presents both repeated “TypeScript” entries and “CoffeeScript” as options.
Ensure the optional multi-selection prompt allows submitting with no tools selected.

report.summary: The release changes canvas selection and paste behavior and alters how imported drawing data is restored.
keyChanges: Shift-clicking an empty canvas area now preserves the current selection instead of clearing it.
Pasted drawings now receive the paste offset directly without subtracting the copied group’s minimum x and y coordinates, changing their final placement.
Loading a file with invalid JSON or no elements now produces an empty drawing instead of leaving the existing drawing in place or failing during parsing.
qaChecks: Verify that Shift-clicking an empty canvas area leaves the existing elements selected.
Check that pasting the copied group applies the paste offset directly to each element’s original coordinates, without subtracting the group’s minimum x and y coordinates.
Verify that loading the valid JSON file with no elements property replaces the existing drawing with an empty canvas.
Check that loading the invalid JSON file resolves to an empty drawing rather than leaving the previous drawing in place.
uncertainty: It is unclear whether the new paste placement is intended; confirm the expected placement for copied groups whose minimum x and y coordinates are nonzero.

report.summary: The release replaces the URL parsing and building behavior, changing how repeated query values and URL composition are handled.
keyChanges: Parsing now preserves repeated query keys as arrays instead of keeping only the last value, so callers can receive every value.
Joining URLs now rejects an appended URL that includes a protocol, rather than combining its path with the base URL.
qaChecks: Verify parsing https://example.test/?tag=one&tag=two retains both tag values in order as ["one","two"].
Verify joining https://example.test/base with https://other.example/path rejects the appended URL with a protocol instead of composing the URLs.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not identify an application page or navigation path where these URL utilities are used.

report.summary: The release adds an on-demand drawing statistics panel and updates how selected objects are targeted by selection controls.
keyChanges: The editor now has a statistics panel showing drawing counts and dimensions, storage sizes, and position and dimensions for selected objects; a single selected object also shows its angle.
Selection controls and sharpness changes now use a plural target-selection helper; the supplied diff does not establish a specific input where this changes the result.
qaChecks: Verify the statistics panel opens from the canvas context menu and can be closed.
Check that with two objects and nothing selected, the panel shows the scene object count, rounded scene width and height, and scene and total storage sizes.
Confirm that selecting one object shows its rounded position, dimensions, and angle, and selecting both shows the selected-object count and their combined rounded bounds.
Test changing sharpness with both objects selected and confirm the change is reflected for the selected objects.
uncertainty: The selection-helper diff is incomplete and provides no concrete input that follows a different path before and after this change, so the expected selection difference and a regression-triggering case cannot be determined from the supplied evidence.

report.summary: Library importing and management have been reorganized across the main editor and embeddable editor API.
keyChanges: The Library file-import action now opens a file picker, but the supplied change does not show the selected file being added; confirm that choosing a library file still imports it.

Library files loaded through the editor’s file-loading flow now merge with existing items and open the Library, while the embeddable editor’s public API replaces URL-specific library importing with library updates.
qaChecks: Verify selecting the .excalidrawlib file adds its item to the existing Library while retaining the item already there.
Check that calling the library-update API with a library item updates the Library and makes the item available for use.
uncertainty: The new file-picker action awaits the selected file but the supplied change does not show it being passed to the Library; selecting a valid library file may therefore fail to add its items.

report.summary: Text sizing and placement have changed across editing, resizing, and drawing output, so verify text remains readable and positioned as expected.
keyChanges: Text size is now measured using font-based dimensions, without the previous baseline measurement or width limit from its container during some updates; this can change wrapping, alignment, and drawing output.
New text no longer receives the previous baseline-based vertical offset, and resizing text now determines font size from width rather than both width and height.
When a word is exactly as wide as the available line, it is now kept as a whole instead of being handled as an over-width word; carriage returns are also normalized when measuring line widths.
For Firefox and Safari, the text editor width gains 0.5 pixels and is no longer capped at the prior maximum width.
qaChecks: Verify a word whose measured width exactly matches the available line width remains together on one line.
Check text copied with Windows-style line endings, such as “first\r\nsecond”, displays as two lines without an extra width or wrapping effect.
Verify newly created text appears at the clicked canvas position without the previous baseline-based vertical offset.
Check editing and then deleting text until only one line remains keeps attached text stable and readable.
Verify resizing a text element and a shape with attached text updates the text size and keeps the text visible.
uncertainty: The previous editing behavior avoided recalculating a bound label’s height on a single line, while the new behavior recalculates it; confirm single-line editing does not cause vertical jumping.

report.summary: This release adds more direct editing of arrow connections and changes how arrow endpoints attach to shapes.
keyChanges: Selected two-point arrows can show draggable focus controls with a dashed guide; dragging a control onto a shape attaches or retargets that endpoint, and Alt switches the binding between inside and orbit modes.
Binding hit testing now includes shape interiors, and endpoint placement no longer applies the previous rectangular-corner adjustment, so corner attachments may land differently.
qaChecks: Verify that hovering over a connected arrow’s focus control highlights it and shows a dashed guide, and that clicking the control directly without first moving the pointer starts dragging it.

Check that dragging one endpoint from the rectangle onto the nearby shape and releasing moves the endpoint’s connection to that shape; then drag it off all shapes and confirm it becomes an unbound endpoint.
Test dragging a connected endpoint while pressing Alt, then release Alt while continuing the drag; confirm the binding switches between inside and orbit placement as the modifier changes.
Confirm that dragging a connected endpoint exactly to a rectangle corner leaves it attached and that the endpoint placement is stable.
uncertainty: The previous rectangular-corner adjustment was removed, but the supplied context does not establish the intended placement at rectangle corners; confirm the expected corner behavior.

checks: Verify that hovering over a connected arrow’s focus control highlights it and shows a dashed guide, and that clicking the control directly without first moving the pointer starts dragging it.

Check that dragging one endpoint from the rectangle onto the nearby shape and releasing moves the endpoint’s connection to that shape; then drag it off all shapes and confirm it becomes an unbound endpoint.
Test dragging a connected endpoint while pressing Alt, then release Alt while continuing the drag; confirm the binding switches between inside and orbit placement as the modifier changes.
Confirm that dragging a connected endpoint exactly to a rectangle corner leaves it attached and that the endpoint placement is stable.

report.summary: This release adds configurable box selection and refines how canvas geometry affects selection, frame contents, and exports.
keyChanges: Box selection now defaults to contain and offers overlap mode, which can select elements when the box crosses their visible outline or attached text rather than fully enclosing them.
Holding Alt and Ctrl/Cmd while dragging can start lasso selection even over the selected elements’ shared bounding area; that area also has extra padding for move-cursor and pointer handling.
Hit testing now accounts for rotated bounds, freehand elements use their bounds center for geometry calculations, and curved-stroke intersection checks allow more iterations.
Frame-based exports and generated frames now use element bounds to identify overlaps while continuing to exclude elements assigned to a different frame.
qaChecks: Verify that with box selection set to overlap, a marquee that crosses the curved stroke’s visible outline but does not contain the whole stroke selects it.
Check the same partial-overlap marquee with box selection set to contain; the element should remain unselected, while a marquee enclosing it should select it.
Test holding Alt and Ctrl/Cmd while dragging over the shared bounding area of already-selected elements; lasso selection should start.
Verify that clicking a visible edge of the rotated shape targets it, while clicking an empty corner of its axis-aligned bounding area does not target it.
Check that an arrow can be connected to the freehand stroke and remains positioned against it when the stroke is moved.
uncertainty: The changed curve-intersection search now allows 10 iterations instead of the old default of 4, but the supplied evidence does not identify a specific user-drawn curve and input that fails with the old limit and succeeds with the new one.

report.summary: The release replaces the URL and query-handling implementation, changing the package’s URL parsing and query capabilities.
keyChanges: URL parsing and formatting now use a replacement URL model, and query parsing and serialization are handled as a separate capability; test URL construction, normalization, and resolution through the package interface.
An empty query key such as the one in ?=x was retained by the previous parser but is now skipped, so it should not appear in parsed query data.
qaChecks: Verify that parsing ?=x produces no query entry for an empty key; the previous behavior retained that entry.
Check that the replacement URL handling returns a formatted URL with its path, query, and fragment preserved for the supplied examples.
uncertainty: The application context does not say whether consumers are expected to retain compatibility with the removed URL and parameter interfaces.
